script.base: Books have CIN leading a high-scoring but not runaway game (implied CIN 26.5 / JAX 23.0). Pace is up with the 49.5 total, but the rush edges split by front quality, not by a shootout.
script.flip1: CIN jumps ahead early, clocks it with Brown, and Burrow/Chase/Higgins stall. Etienne's carries die as JAX abandons the run. Brown over and Etienne rush under both get safer; JAX pass-catcher overs would be the correlated add, not a second rush leg.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because week-1 samples lied. CIN's 2.04 YPC was a bad rushing opponent, Etienne broke another 40-plus run on 18 carries, and 143.5 got there on one play the same way 16/143 did. On the other leg JAX's 4.75 YPC was a mobile quarterback, not a structural front leak, Brown stayed at 2 yards a carry on 18 rushes, and 43.5 missed by a nose while Perine took the goal-line series. The stand-in prices were never real closes, so a 'win' against 143.5 would not have been CLV. Weather, uncharted, could also have turned the outdoor game into a slog that caps Brown without saving a bad Etienne explosive.
slip_story: One story: CIN controls the trenches in a 26.5-23.0 game. Brown rush over rides the favorite carry script into JAX's soft front; Etienne rush under fades the dog run game into CIN's stuffed front with Milum out. Do not add Chase/Higgins/Thomas overs — those need a pass script and a CB scratch that is still only Doubtful. No TDs, one market per player, two legs.
